segments: 4620/01: How would you grow a motorcycle brand that's about to shut down?
4620/02: This is a real BCG interview question.
4620/04: YokLind is a 100 year old motorcycle company.
4620/05: Its factory can make 6000 bikes a month.
4620/06: but it's selling only 2000.
4620/07: the board is thinking about shutting it down.

4620/49: Put rental bikes in Goa Manali and Lay.

4620/56: new products for the same customers.
4620/59: Why don't people buy? Because it's heavy, it breaks down and the gear is on the opposite side from every other bike.
4621/04: So fix exactly that, fix the reliability.
4621/06: and make a lighter version but keep the thumb, the shape and the history because that's the reason anyone buys it at all so we don't want to let go of the legacy.
4621/07: Fourth, new products for new customers. Sell accessories like...
4621/08: riding jackets, helmets, saddlebags and custom parts through dealers and online.
4621/09: Every bike already on the road becomes a customer again.
4621/10: So, I'd start with the first two because they don't need new factory or new product. I'd fix the bike in parallel and add accessory in the existing dealers once the brand is growing again.
